source.title: A Performance Comparison of Different YOLOv7 Networks for High-Accuracy Cell Classification in Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid Utilising the Adam Optimiser and Label Smoothing
source.authors: Sebastian Rumpf; N. Zufall; Florian Rumpf; Andreas Gschwendtner

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper. The published-version notice and preprint metadata are both included.
record.tranche_reason: Compares Adam with the default optimizer on BAL cell detection using held-out performance metrics, but pairs Adam with label smoothing and does not isolate the optimizer effect.
record.gate_note: The study tests four YOLOv7 variants on a held-out test set. It reports no significant differences among them. Adam is combined with label smoothing, so its separate effect cannot be determined. The paper cites prior work on adaptive optimizers; cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out performance under SGD and Adam-based training in a new medical-image detection setting, bearing on V4. Adam is always introduced together with label smoothing, so the comparison tests a bundled recipe and cannot isolate the optimizer's effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' interpretation: neither Adam nor label smoothing improved their results, and default YOLOv7 offered similarly strong performance with lower computational demands than E6E. Their experiments establish only the joint intervention's performance. They also conclude that automated BAL analysis is promising but requires further validation for clinical use and more diverse data.
record.recipe_differences: Uses YOLOv7 object detection on BAL cytology images and compares Adam plus label smoothing against default training; it does not use the original claim's random-label or generalization-gap protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: The YOLOv7-E6E batch size was 32 versus 56 for YOLOv7 due to memory limitations; the authors attribute architecture differences to scaling and note that their classification problem may be too simple to benefit from increased width and depth.
record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine
record.problems: The Adam comparison is confounded with label smoothing. The study has no cross-validation, and training and test mosaics were drawn from the same digitized cytospin preparations. The paper notes that additional validation on more diverse data is needed.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 separately reports class-specific values for four models across five measures. These 80 class-specific entries are not extracted; the 20 rows retained cover the across-class means and all reported mean measures relevant to V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width variation beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold under otherwise comparable training.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

The isolated optimizer effect, matched training performance, learning-rate and schedule searches, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and language benchmarks. Stock hyperparameters were used rather than a documented optimizer-specific tuning comparison.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout interventions, including interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps and comparisons with alternative measures.
Memorization-based example removal and retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. All reported uncertainties are across-class SDs, not estimates of training-run variability. Non-significant omnibus tests do not establish equivalence. Training and test tiles came from the same cytospin preparations, and no cross-validation was performed. Class-specific results are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare natural-label and random-label test performance.
Does not measure training error or test error around an interpolation threshold; YOLOv7-E6E differs in more than width.
All tested models are convolutional; there is no fully connected comparator.
Does not isolate Adam from label smoothing, test broader hyperparameter tuning, switching to SGD, decoupled weight decay, or language benchmarks.
Does not compare batch sizes under a fixed epoch budget; batch size differs between YOLOv7 and YOLOv7-E6E.
Does not test dropout or its combination with weight decay and data augmentation.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or relate it to a training-test gap.
Does not remove memorized training examples or measure the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: YOLOv7 and YOLOv7-E6E on BAL cell detection, using stock training settings and adding Adam together with label smoothing
relationships.reason: R1–R20 report no significant four-network differences across five held-out metrics, providing no demonstrated adaptive-method penalty in this bundled-recipe setting; the confound and omnibus tests prevent an optimizer-specific conclusion.
relationships.display_finding: Reported tests find no significant differences across the networks, but verification remains incomplete. Label smoothing was included in the optimizer comparison, preventing a conclusion about the optimizer alone.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: BAL cell classification with Adam combined with label smoothing, compared with default YOLOv7 and YOLOv7-E6E
reader_labels.reason: Across the reported held-out metrics, the paper reports no significant differences among the four variants; the joint Adam and label-smoothing change does not isolate either component (R1–R20).
